methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prospective, open-label, randomized phase III trial across 57 centers comparing mFOLFOXIRI/panitumumab versus mFOLFOX/panitumumab in RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC with stratified 1:1 assignment (Methods; Study Design). Endpoints are prespecified with an ITT primary analysis for ORR and time-to-event secondary endpoints including OS and PFS (Abstract; Methods; Statistical Analyses). The analysis includes a priori power calculation for the primary endpoint and standard survival methods (Kaplan-Meier, HRs with 95% CIs), but the normalized text references additional details in an Appendix, and open-label design can introduce bias for some assessments (Methods).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The trial tests a frontline regimen strategy for metastatic colorectal cancer and reports long-term overall survival, which is directly practice-relevant (Abstract; Introduction). As an individual randomized phase III trial, it maps to Oxford LoE 1b (Methods). The clinical effect is meaningful but should be interpreted alongside the negative primary endpoint (no ORR improvement) and borderline OS significance (Abstract).

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is applicable for this randomized trial, and the manuscript reports trial registration (ClinicalTrials.gov), randomization/stratification, primary/secondary endpoints, follow-up, and key effect estimates (Methods; Abstract). However, several operational details are noted as previously published or in an Appendix (online only), limiting completeness in the normalized text (Methods). No explicit data or code availability statement is present in the normalized manuscript, so reproducibility support appears limited here.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is positioned as the first phase III randomized evaluation of adding irinotecan (mFOLFOXIRI) to an anti-EGFR backbone versus doublet control in this population (Introduction). While the primary activity endpoint (ORR) was not improved at earlier analysis, the final report adds mature OS follow-up and detailed post-progression treatment accounting (Abstract). Overall, this is a meaningful but not paradigm-shifting extension in an established treatment area.

writing_presentation.justification: The Abstract clearly reports randomized groups, sample sizes, follow-up duration, and effect sizes with CIs and P values for OS and other endpoints. Methods outline design, stratification, power assumptions, and statistical tests in a standard format (Methods; Statistical Analyses). The normalized text appears to truncate some details to an Appendix, but the main presentation remains clear and publication-ready.

key_strengths: Large multicenter randomized phase III design with prespecified endpoints and power calculation for ORR.
Provides mature long-term OS follow-up and detailed subsequent-therapy context.
Clear reporting of effect sizes (HRs, 95% CIs) for key time-to-event endpoints.
key_concerns: Primary endpoint (ORR) was not met and most secondary efficacy endpoints (PFS/ETS/DoR/R0) were not improved, complicating interpretation of the OS signal.
Open-label design and reliance on Appendix/previous publications for some details limits evaluability from the normalized text alone.
No explicit data/code sharing statement is present in the normalized manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-conducted randomized trial with clinically relevant long-term outcomes, but the discordance between a negative primary endpoint and a modest OS benefit supports a mid–high tier placement with substantial revision-level scrutiny.
